claims.text: The nanoparticles are equimolar CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy nanoparticles synthesized by colloidal methods.
The initial CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles are crystallized as a single-phase solid solution.
Annealing in a mildly oxidizing atmosphere forms an in situ sub-nanometer oxide passivation layer.
Annealing at 600–800 K facilitates formation of the oxide passivation layer.
The oxide passivation layer acts as a diffusion barrier.
The oxide layer minimizes atomic diffusion during subsequent high-temperature operation.
Reducing atomic diffusion minimizes surface segregation in CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles.
Suppressing diffusion and surface segregation maintains the original single-phase structure and chemical homogeneity.
Passivated nanoparticles will retain solid-solution integrity across reactive operating conditions spanning 473–1923 K.
Passivated nanoparticles will show less elemental segregation than inert-annealed controls.
Nanoparticles annealed in an inert atmosphere will show early phase separation and surface segregation during high-temperature exposure.
The protective mechanism remains effective only while the oxide passivation layer remains stable.
Excessive oxide-layer thickening can alter catalytic performance.
Significant degradation or evolution of the oxide layer before 1923 K may diminish its protective effect.
